brief_item.title: GPU时序图聚类将社区检测转为池化原语
brief_item.direction_name: 加速器、内存、存储与AI Fabric
brief_item.core_conclusion: 该工作把时序图社区检测和池化做成GPU稀疏计算原语，用对称Bethe-Hessian替代难以GPU化的非对称算子。A100对CPU等工作量比较最高约978倍，但下游池化是否保留时间依赖仍未验证。
brief_item.mechanism: GPU后端在稀疏supra-adjacency上执行多层模块度与谱计算，Bethe-Hessian负特征值恢复信息方向，并通过NetworkX-Temporal环境变量切换CPU/GPU。
brief_item.result: 五次、两迭代匹配预算且含主机到设备传输的测试中，Patent约978倍、ArxivAI 64倍、ArxivCS 31倍、ArxivMath 30倍。硬件为Xeon Gold 6330与A100 80GB。
brief_item.boundary: 速度依赖数据密度、快照数和硬件，不代表多GPU或下游模型收益。方法主要适用于无向图，时序有向算子、能耗和故障恢复未测。
brief_item.project_relevance: 可用于压缩仓库历史或Agent交互图，再交给下游学习。落地需测图更新、显存、池化保真度和时间依赖保留，不能把单A100加速直接视为Agent端到端收益。

facts.title: Learning and Clustering on Temporal Graphs: Principles, Primitives, and Pooling
facts.event_hint: arXiv:2608.03696v1 presents GPU temporal-graph clustering as a scalable, theory-grounded pooling primitive
facts.problem: Temporal graph clustering can provide coarse-grained representations for graph learning, but CPU methods become impractical as node and snapshot counts grow. It is also unclear when neural graph models outperform principled algorithmic clustering, especially when attributes are weak or absent.
facts.mechanism: The work combines three views: detectability theory for temporal community structure, GPU-accelerated multislice modularity and spectral primitives over sparse supra-adjacency representations, and community assignments as a pooling/coarse-graining operator. Because the informative non-backtracking operator is asymmetric and difficult for GPU sparse eigensolvers, the implementation reformulates it through the symmetric Bethe-Hessian H(r), whose negative eigenvalues recover informative directions for undirected graphs. The backend is exposed through NetworkX-Temporal with a single environment-variable switch from CPU to GPU.

evidence.claim: Against an equal-work CPU reference, the GPU multislice modularity backend achieved speedups up to roughly three orders of magnitude, depending on graph density and snapshot count.
evidence.baseline: CPU reference under an equal-work budget
evidence.condition: Temporal graph datasets with varying density and number of snapshots; speedup is workload-dependent.

evidence.claim: The runtime figure reports GPU/CPU ratios including approximately 978× on Patent, 64× on ArxivAI, 31× on ArxivCS, and 30× on ArxivMath; static Cora and CiteSeer cases are not representative temporal workloads.
evidence.condition: Matched two-iteration budget, five runs, including host-to-device transfer.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.3, Figure 1 and runtime table

evidence.claim: The comparison uses an Intel Xeon Gold 6330 CPU and NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU; the datasets range from 2,708 nodes/5 snapshots to 270,013 unique nodes and 31 snapshots.
evidence.condition: Dataset/runtime table in Figure 1; values include unique and snapshot-summed nodes/edges.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.3, Figure 1 caption and dataset table

evidence.claim: The symmetric Bethe-Hessian reformulation preserves asymptotic optimality for undirected graphs while keeping matrix operations GPU-compatible, avoiding the asymmetric non-backtracking eigensolver limitation.
evidence.condition: Theoretical/algorithmic construction; temporal regularization still depends jointly on community signal λ and persistence η.

evidence.claim: The authors frame community detection as a principled pooling assignment, but warn that temporal pooling may fail to preserve ordered dependencies when co-membership alone is insufficient.
evidence.baseline: Heuristic or learned graph pooling without guarantees
evidence.condition: Conceptual pooling interpretation; downstream task preservation is identified as an open problem.

facts.evaluation_context: This is a short theoretical-and-systems paper with GPU runtime evidence from temporal and static graph datasets. The runtime comparison uses a matched two-iteration Leiden budget, five runs, an Intel Xeon Gold 6330 CPU, and an NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU, including host-to-device transfer. The backend uses CuPy/RAPIDS and NetworkX-Temporal, while the paper discusses detectability under stochastic block models and graph-pooling implications rather than an end-to-end GNN benchmark.
facts.limitations: The reported speedups are for the authors' implementation, equal-work budget, selected datasets, and A100/Xeon hardware; they do not establish equivalent gains on other GPUs, multi-GPU systems, dynamic update patterns, or downstream model quality. The Bethe-Hessian construction addresses undirected graph spectral compatibility, while asymmetric temporal operators and attributed regularization remain open engineering/theory issues. Community-based pooling may lose temporally ordered dependencies, and the paper provides no failure-recovery, energy, or production deployment measurements.
facts.project_relevance: The result is a plausible GPU primitive for compressing temporal dependency graphs, repository histories, or agent interaction networks before downstream learning. Its main practical signal is that host-to-device-inclusive clustering can move some temporal workloads from CPU-intractable to routine on GPU, but a target system still needs to measure graph-update cost, memory footprint, pooling fidelity, and whether coarse-graining preserves the temporal dependencies the agent actually uses.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF was fetched and the title matches the input metadata exactly.
Runtime numbers are reported with hardware, iteration, run-count, and dataset conditions; no universal speedup is inferred.
